genZNote: Usually a normal gut resident, but some strains really said: let me ruin your week.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Lower intestinal tract of warm-blooded animals, including humans
habitat.hostAssociation: Normal gut flora; certain strains (e.g. enterotoxigenic, enterohemorrhagic) are pathogenic
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Found in water and soil contaminated with fecal matter; used as a standard indicator organism for fecal contamination

culture.media: MacConkey agar, EMB (eosin methylene blue) agar
culture.growthCharacteristics: Rapid growth, facultative anaerobe, grows well at 37°C
culture.colonyMorphology: Large, gray, mucoid colonies on nutrient agar
culture.pigmentation: None; green metallic sheen on EMB agar
culture.hemolysis: Variable — some strains beta-hemolytic on blood agar

identificationClues: Lactose fermenter — pink colonies on MacConkey agar
Green metallic sheen on EMB agar

clinicalImportance.transmission: Fecal-oral route for pathogenic strains; endogenous spread from the patient's own gut flora in most UTIs
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Leading cause of community- and hospital-acquired UTIs worldwide; O157:H7 is associated with undercooked beef and unpasteurized dairy
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Standard indicator organism for fecal contamination of water supplies

examFacts.importantTest: IMViC pattern (+ + − −); green sheen on EMB agar
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Lactose fermentation plus indole positivity separates it from Salmonella and Shigella
